source_quote:
Employee benefits normally considered chargeable to a Joint Account are detailed in COPAS MFI-27, Employee Benefits and Percentage Limitation.

Charges may be made to the Joint Account for benefit plans expenses on a "when and as paid" basis or by "percentage assessment on the amount of the labor costs. It is generally agreed that the "percentage assessment" provides a more equitable distribution of these costs. If the "percentage assessment" method is used, it should be based on the Operator's actual cost experience, however, the application of a rate determined from the preceding year's experience may be considered as compliance with the "current cost  requirement. Under either method the Operator's own cost of administering such plans should be excluded. In determination of actual cost experience, any dividends or refunds received which are applicable to insurance or annuity policies should be used to reduce the cost of such policies.

Costs which are primarily beneficial to the Operator should be excluded from employee benefits and treated as overhead, for which the Operator is compensated under the provisions of Section III. source_quote:
(1) “Salaries and wages of Operator's field employees directly employed on the Joint Property in
the conduct of Joint Operations.”

Field employees are defined as employees below First Level Supervisor directly employed
on the Joint Property. In most instances the original time sheets or some other written
documentation should show the time spent on any particular job or Joint Property; and the
charge should be based upon such time shown. in some instances, however, certain
employees may directly serve a number of properties, each having one or more wells, and it
may not be practical nor equitable to use time as a basis for the charge due to location of
employees' headquarters (dog houses, etc.), travel time required, common facilities serving
properties manned by the employee and other reasons. In such instances, it is sometimes more
feasible to allocate the charge to all properties served on a well, or other equitable basis, than
on the time spent on the individual properties.

allowances are recognized Joint Account costs, chargeable on a "when and as paid" basis or by

costs. It is recommended that the "percentage assessment" be reviewed currently and that proper
adjustments be made in the rate to provide, over a period of time, that actual costs are distributed

determining the new adjusted rate.

conditions: Charges must represent a complete and accurate allocation of costs, exclude profit and duplication, and be supported by third-party invoices or documentation; audit depends on whether charges are based on Cost Basis or Negotiated Rate Basis.
exceptions: If based on Negotiated Rate Basis, audit limited to verifying agreed rates and correct units; if based on Cost Basis, audit includes books and annual attestation.
required_support: Invoices from Affiliate’s third-party vendors, auditable records, annual report from independent public accounting firm, supporting documentation.
source_quote: The audit procedures for Affiliate costs will depend on whether they were charged based on the Cost Basis or the Negotiated Rate Basis. (Refer to Section II.7.A.) If the Cost Basis was used, the Parties wanting to verify the costs will be allowed to audit the Affiliate’s books related to the charges to the Joint Account, or the Party providing the Affiliate will provide the annual attestation described in this Section I.5.F. If the Affiliate supplies an annual attestation, the other Parties may still audit the books of the Party providing the Affiliate to verify that the hours billed by the Affiliate are correct. This can include reviewing to ensure the Affiliate/Non-Operator did not bill duplicate hours, the person was performing a billable function, and that the work performed was in scope. If the Negotiated Rate Basis is used, the auditing Parties will verify that the rates charged were as agreed and that the hours billed are correct. The audit may include verifying: (i) there were no duplicate charges, (ii) the charges do not include personnel who performed overhead functions, and (iii) the work performed was in scope.

required_support: Documentation of charges consistent with referenced sections; may require approval if included in rates.
source_quote:
Affiliate employee charges related to Personal Expenses, training, and awards shall be made in the same manner as provided for employees in Sections II.2.D, II.2.E, and II.2.G.

The Operator might provide training or awards to an entire Feasibility Team or Project Team or subsets of the team (e.g., the group working on the topsides).  In that case, the Operator would directly charge the cost to the Joint Account, rather than billing the portion of the costs attributable to Affiliate team members to the various Affiliates, to include in their rates.  Also, the Operator could provide training to Non-Operator Affiliates, not just the Operator’s Affiliates, so these costs could also be a direct charge to the Joint Account.  Thus, this provision could apply regardless of whether the Affiliate is billed on a Cost Basis or at a negotiated rate.  However, if the training or awards are provided by the Affiliate, the costs could be rolled into its rate calculation in the Cost Basis (and may or may not be included in the case of negotiated rates.)

source_quote:
(1) Preparation Costs
Costs to prepare Material for use, including, but not limited to inspection, third-party surveillance, sandblasting, stenciling, perforating and coating  will be charged to the Joint Account at prices which reflect the  actual costs of the services, in accordance with Section II (Direct Charges).  Preparation costs incurred will not be credited for new unused Material transferred from the Joint Account unless these services permanently alter Material and provide full value to any future receiving property.

The cost to prepare Material means the actual costs paid to a third party, less any discounts or rebates received, or an average cost or rate for a warehouse location for preparing Material for use by the Joint Account.  If a Party or an Affiliate performed any of the Material preparation work, the provisions of Section II, pertaining to labor, Materials, etc. apply to the preparation costs.  The Operator must provide documentation, upon request, to support preparation costs charged to the Joint Account.  If the preparation costs pertained to more than one property, the documentation must include information to support the method of allocating such charges.  Preparation costs charged to the Joint Account cannot include costs classified as overhead under Section III (Overhead).

This is common practice because of accounting system limitations, ease of administration, and to protect the employee’s privacy.  There are several factors to consider in computing this day rate, or other time equivalent rate (hourly rate or monthly rate): The rate should be based on a group of employees performing similar job functions. required_support: Operator actual benefit-cost basis and the applicable COPAS-recommended percentage for the year.
source_quote: The COPAS intent in establishing an employee benefits limit each year is twofold: (1) to place a ceiling on the amount the operator may charge for employee benefits and (2) to provide for automatic revision of this ceiling, based on an annual industry survey of these costs, without formally amending the agreements.
source_evidence_context: MFI-14 caps employee-benefit charges at the operator's actual cost, not exceeding the COPAS-recommended percentage, which is auto-revised annually.

advisor_rule_title: Affiliate charges limited to actual cost; discounts pass through
advisor_scope_reason: Primary 1986 Offshore COPAS authority aligned to the governing Exhibit C accounting procedure.
source_doc: MFI-18-Operator-Affililates-and-Related-Entities.pdf
conditions: Goods/services from Operator Related Entities are chargeable, but must not exceed actual cost; trade and other discounts must be passed through to the joint account.
exceptions: Rates provided in the COPAS model form accounting procedures govern where applicable, rather than commercial/marked-up rates.
required_support: Related-entity actual cost and evidence discounts were passed through.
source_quote: An operator may have Related Entities from which they purchase materials such as tubular goods, wellhead equipment, mud, bits, fuel, etc., at prices which are higher than those paid by the Related Entity... because trade or other discounts are not passed on to the joint account or the operator simply marks-up the price paid to the actual outside supplier.
source_evidence_context: MFI-18 identifies improper affiliate charging (marked-up prices, unremitted discounts, commercial rates in excess of actual cost) and requires charges to reflect actual cost.

advisor_rule_title: Employee benefits chargeable subject to percentage limitation and agreement precedence
advisor_scope_reason: Primary 1986 Offshore COPAS authority aligned to the governing Exhibit C accounting procedure.
source_doc: MFI-27-Employee-Benefits-and-Percentage-Limitation.pdf
conditions: Employee benefits recouped by applying a percentage representative of the operator's actual cost to chargeable salaries/wages; subject to the applicable contract limitation (often the COPAS-recommended percentage).
exceptions: The joint operating agreement, accounting procedure, and other relevant agreements take precedence where they conflict with this interpretation.
required_support: Benefit-rate build-up and reconciliation to actual cost; applicable contractual limitation.
source_quote: The operator recoups these employee benefits costs by applying a percentage, representative of the operator's actual cost of providing the employee benefits, to chargeable personnel's salaries and wages... the employee benefits percentage applied to labor charges may be subject to limitations under the applicable contract.

advisor_rule_title: Incentive compensation (ICP) directly chargeable on same basis as salary
advisor_scope_reason: Primary 1986 Offshore COPAS authority aligned to the governing Exhibit C accounting procedure.
source_doc: MFI-37-Incentive-Compensation-Costs.pdf
conditions: Cash ICPs are directly chargeable to the joint account for employees whose salaries/wages are chargeable, on the same basis as salary, and only to the extent time is directly chargeable; must be a formally documented operator policy.
exceptions: ICP for time not charged to the joint account is not chargeable; awards that are not ICP may fall to overhead (see MFI-49).
required_support: Documented ICP policy and allocation tying the award to chargeable salary/time.
source_quote: COPAS recommends that ICPs paid in cash be directly charged to the joint account for employees whose salaries and wages are chargeable pursuant to the prevailing accounting procedure/operating agreement... Such programs must be a formally documented policy of the operator.
source_evidence_context: MFI-37 makes documented cash ICPs directly chargeable in proportion to chargeable salary; undocumented or non-chargeable-time ICP is not chargeable.

advisor_rule_title: Shorebase costs chargeable; exclude overhead-covered and non-shorebase costs
advisor_scope_reason: Primary 1986 Offshore COPAS authority aligned to the governing Exhibit C accounting procedure.
source_doc: MFI-46-Shorebase-Facilities-and-Offshore-Staging-Areas.pdf
source_section: IV. Costs Included in Shorebase Operations
conditions: Direct operating costs of shorebase facilities/services are chargeable; a rate to recover cost of ownership may also be charged per the Operator-owned facilities provision.
exceptions: Exclude costs covered by overhead (office/warehouse space and personnel) and costs allocated from higher organizational levels that do not apply to shorebase operations.
required_support: Shorebase cost build-up and allocation method (time-writing, crane usage, equivalent active completion, or marine activity).
source_quote: Care should be taken to exclude costs which may occur at a Shorebase Facility location or are allocated to a Shorebase from a higher organizational level, and that do not apply to Shorebase Facility operations (e.g., warehouse space, office space and operating costs for field operating personnel, warehousing personnel and other charges covered by overhead).
source_evidence_context: MFI-46 limits shorebase charges to direct shorebase operating costs plus a cost-of-ownership rate, and requires exclusion of overhead-covered items.

advisor_rule_title: Drilling overhead commencement/termination by spud and rig-release
advisor_scope_reason: Primary 1986 Offshore COPAS authority aligned to the governing Exhibit C accounting procedure.
source_doc: MFI-48-Application-and-Calculation-of-Drilling-Overhead.pdf
source_section: II. Combined Fixed Rate Overhead — Commencement/Termination
conditions: Combined fixed-rate drilling overhead commences on the spud date and terminates when the drilling or completion rig is released, whichever is later; offshore uses equipment-on/off-location dates.
exceptions: No charges during suspension of operations for 15 or more consecutive days; provisions differ by COPAS edition.
required_support: Spud date, rig-release date, and applicable COPAS edition's drilling-overhead provision.
source_quote: COPAS '62 Drilling — Spud date ... Date drilling or completion rig released, whichever is later. ... Offshore & inland waters drilling — Date drilling or completion equipment arrives on location ... moves off location or is released, whichever is first. ... Except no charges during suspension of operations for 15 or more consecutive days.

advisor_rule_title: Awards not qualifying as salary/ICP/benefits are Operator overhead
advisor_scope_reason: Primary 1986 Offshore COPAS authority aligned to the governing Exhibit C accounting procedure.
source_doc: MFI-49 Employee and Contractor Awards.pdf
conditions: Safety awards, service awards and similar awards primarily beneficial to the operator are treated as Overhead (for which the operator is compensated), not as a direct charge.
exceptions: Awards paid to contractors may be chargeable under the Services provision; project/operational awards tied to chargeable labor may follow the underlying labor treatment.
required_support: Award type and basis; demonstration it is not primarily beneficial to the operator.
source_quote: Some Awards do not qualify as salaries and wages, ICP, or employee benefits, nor do they qualify as a Direct Charge under any other Direct Charge provisions of the Accounting Procedure. Consequently, these Awards are considered Overhead. ... Such costs to be borne by the Operator would include ...safety awards, service awards, ...and other special benefits available only to executives, certain employees or groups on a selective basis.
source_evidence_context: MFI-49 classifies safety/service awards primarily benefiting the operator as Overhead (not directly chargeable); contractor awards may be chargeable under Services.
resolved_reference_text: MFI-49 classifies safety/service awards primarily benefiting the operator as Overhead (not directly chargeable); contractor awards may be chargeable under Services.
